main_body: Tall Parisian-style shop building: slate mansard roof with two dormers and a chimney, an orange cornice, a brick facade with four lit windows per floor, a balcony rail, and a striped awning over a shopfront.
top_band: Column x=32: row 16 is the dark outline, rows 17-23 are a lighter blue-grey roof-top band (L 95-122, 7 rows). Rows 24-43 are the darker slate mansard slope (L 50-103), and rows 44-46 are the orange cornice.
evidence: The roof reads as a roof. A flat deck band at rows 17-23 has a lighter 1-row edge at row 23 and a dark shadow row at 24, which leads into the scaled slate slope at rows 25-43 with dormers and a chimney. The orange cornice (rows 44-46) caps the wall like an eave. The wall below is a front face with window surrounds, sills, a balcony and an awning, so the facade is vertical, as it is on the Beodeul house references. The step between the deck band and the slope is only about 8-20 L, which is weak, but the sloped slate area is a clear roof surface above the front face and the structure matches the reference houses.

style.evidence: Shading and texture are good. The slate has scale rows in about 5 greys. The brick has per-brick variation. The windows have warm glow dots, and the cornice, awning and balcony carry detail. Colours per tile are 14, between the references' 18 and 11, and flat-fill coverage is 2%. The weak point is the outline. 97% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral (about #1d1722), against 7-9% for both references, whose outlines lean toward the neighbouring material. The candidate also has only 54 distinct colours against 185 and 66. The building is rich internally, but the uniform near-black edge gives it the sticker look the standard rejects.
